title: A class diagram for hostel bookings
instructions:
## From nouns to classes

From the requirements: a **Student** (with an index number and name) makes **Bookings**; each Booking is for one **Room** in one **Hostel**, for an academic year, and has a status. A Hostel contains many Rooms (a room cannot exist without its hostel). A Room has a number and a capacity. Both students and hostel officers are **Persons** with a name and email; an **Officer** has a staff id.

## Do this

Write the class diagram:

- five or more classes with their attributes (use `+name: type`), and at least one operation such as `+book(room)` on Student;
- Person as the superclass of Student and Officer;
- Student `1` to `*` Booking; Room `1` to `*` Booking; Hostel to Room as **composition**, `1` to `*`.
hints: Person <|-- Student draws the inheritance arrow from Student to Person.
Student "1" -- "*" Booking : makes gives the multiplicities on each end.
Hostel "1" *-- "*" Room is composition: the filled diamond sits at the Hostel end.

checks.label: Every class has members and is related to another

realityNote: A domain class diagram like this one maps almost directly to database tables or to classes in Java or Python; the multiplicities become foreign keys and collections. Composition versus aggregation is about lifetime: delete the hostel and its rooms go with it.
